The Construction sector displays a trend where the higher the industry concentration ratio the lower the proportion of workers with higher qualifications. In terms of distribution the Construction sector is evenly distributed across England and Wales though local authorities in London are seen to have a generally lower industry concentration. 
The two local authorities where the Construction industry employs the highest percentage of workers are Castle Point and Maldon. Construction in Castle Point employs 14.45%  of the workforce, in Maldon it is 14.36%, compared to 8.66%   in England and Wales  . 
However, of those working in Construction, 15.19%   in Castle Point and 17.15% in Maldon have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 14 and 12 percentage points below the sector average of 29.70%. 
The two local authorities where the Construction sector employs the lowest percentage of workers are Tower Hamlets and Kensington and Chelsea.   Only 3.16%  of the people who live in Tower Hamlets and 3.31% of people in Kensington and Chelsea and work in Construction, compared to the England and Wales average of 8.66%. 
However, of those working in Construction, 45.38% in Tower Hamlets and 43.46% in Kensington and Chelsea have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 13 percentage points 9 percentage points above the sector average of 29.70%.
Nearly 12.76% of workers in the Construction sector have apprenticeships as their highest qualification. This is the highest of all industry sectors and is more than twice the average for England and Wales across all industries (5%).  The Local Authorities with the highest proportion of workers in construction who have come through apprenticeships were South Lakeland, Scarborough and Swansea (19%, 18.5% and 18% respectively). 
Sectors that display the same trend of higher concentrated industries having lower qualified workers include Manufacturing, Agriculture, forestry and fishing and Wholesale and retail.
Almost 50% of people working in Construction work in ‘Skilled trades occupations’. 
The occupations in the construction sector with the highest proportion of worker with higher qualifications are Quantity surveyors (80.4%) and Engineering professionals (77.5%).

The occupations in the Construction sector with the most workers are Production manager and directors in construction (11.1%) and Construction and building trades (8.3%). Both occupations have a relatively low proportion of workers with higher qualifications.

The Wholesale and retail sector which includes the repair of motor vehicles and motor cycles, displays a trend where the higher the industry concentration the lower the proportion of workers with higher qualifications. The sector also tends to be more highly concentrated outside London.
Sectors that display the same trend of higher concentrated industries having lower qualified workers include Manufacturing, Construction and Agriculture, forestry, and fishing.
The two local authorities where the Wholesale sector employs the highest percentage of workers are Tamworth and Doncaster. Wholesale in Tamworth employs 21.40% of the workforce, in Doncaster it is 21.11%, compared to 14.96% in England and Wales.
However, of those working in Wholesale, 18.42% in Tamworth and 18.71% in Doncaster have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 10 and 11percentage points above the sector average of 29.70%. The two local authorities where the Wholesale sector employs the lowest percentage of workers are Cambridge and Oxford. Only 8.60% of the people who live in Wandsworth and 9.29% of people in Cambridge work in Oxford, compared to the England and Wales average of 14.96%.
However, of those working in Wholesale, 38.92% in Cambridge and 31.07% in Oxford have higher education qualifications, 9 and 1 percentage points respectively above the industry average of 29.70%.
Local authorities in London tend to have a higher proportion of workers in Wholesale and retail with higher qualifications than elsewhere in England and Wales. For example, Kingston upon Thames and Cardiff have approximately the same industry concentration, however Kingston upon Thames has a proportion of workers with higher qualifications of 43.55% while in Cardiff the proportion of worker with higher qualifications is 29.91%.
The occupations in the Wholesale and retail sector with the highest proportion of workers with higher qualifications are Optometrists (95.6%) and Chartered and certified accountants (92.8%).
The occupations in the Wholesale and retail sector with the most workers are Sales and retail assistants (23.9%) and Managers and directors in retail and wholesale (10.3%). Both these occupations have a relatively low proportion of workers with higher qualifications. Managers being one of the most common occupations is due senior positions in wholesale and retail being grouped together whilst junior roles are allocated to more specific occupations.

The Education sector has a more even distribution of qualification levels across England and Wales, the industry concentration ratios are much closer to 1, showing that the proportion of workers in each area working in Education is similar to the proportion in England and Wales.
Sectors like Education that don’t display a clear trend when it comes to the concentration of an industry and the proportion of workers who have higher qualifications include Human health and social work activities and Administrative and support services.
The two local authorities where the Education industry employs the highest percentage of workers are Richmond Upon Thames and Cambridge. Education in Richmond Upon Thames employs 11.84% of the workforce, in Cambridge it is 21.46%, compared to 9.84%   in England and Wales  . 
However, of those working in Education, 79.65%   in Richmond Upon Thames and 79.27% in Cambridge have higher education qualifications. Respectively, these are 49 percentage points and 9 percentage points above the sector average of 29.70%.
The two local authorities where the Education sector employs the lowest percentage of workers are Crawley and Boston.   Only 6.3% of the people who live in Crawley and 6.34% of people in Boston work in Education, compared to the England and Wales average of 9.84%. 
However, of those working in Education, 50.07%  in Crawley and 50.47%  in West Minster have higher education qualifications, Respectively, these are both 49 percentage points above the sector average of 29.70%. 
Cambridge and Oxford are the only two local authorities where the industry concentration ratio exceeds 2, with 2.2 and 2.4 respectively. This is likely due to their universities, two of the most recognised and respected institutions in the world, hiring numerous researchers and professionals and attracting scholars and academics. Their proportion of workers with higher education is also two of the highest 77.76% and 79.26% respectively. 
The pattern of local authorities with large universities for their population size having higher industry concentration and higher education levels is seen in other areas. Ceredigion and Canterbury both have Education industry density greater than average (1.32 and 1.62) and higher education levels greater than the national proportion (65%) at 71.54% and 70.48% respectively. This is likely due to the presence of Aberystwyth University and Kent University in these areas.
The occupations in the Education sector with the highest proportion of workers with higher qualifications are Headteachers and principals (96.9%) and Higher education teaching professionals (96.7%).
The occupations in the Education sector with the most workers are Secondary education teaching professionals (11.0%) and Primary education teaching professionals (10.6%). Both occupations have a very higher proportion of workers with higher qualifications.
